- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overpredict early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish — adjust downward by 2–5% for days 1–7.  
- After a strong price spike (e.g., >70), forecast often overshoots the true value — cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10% below the spike peak.  
- Mean reversion is strong in the last 7–10 days — if forecast is trending upward beyond 68.5, apply a downward correction of 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), forecast should be smoother — dampen volatility by averaging 2–3 consecutive days’ forecast values.
